title: TAM SAM SOM: Sizing Any Market
description: Practice breaking down markets using TAM, SAM, and SOM frameworks with real-world scenarios.

interactions.prompt: The total revenue opportunity if 100% of the world's potential customers bought your product is called the ____.

options.text: Serviceable Addressable Market (SAM)
Total Addressable Market (TAM)
Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM)
Market Penetration Rate

interactions.prompt: A pet food startup reports: US pet food market = $50B (TAM), premium organic segment = $8B (SAM), Year 1 target = $12M (SOM). Their SOM is 0.15% of SAM. What stands out?

options.text: TAM is too large to be useful
SOM at 0.15% of SAM is a realistic Year 1 target
SAM should be larger than $8B
They should target the full TAM immediately

chartData.title: Pet Food Startup Market Analysis ($B vs $M)

data.name: TAM: Total US Pet Food Market

interactions.prompt: You're sizing the US electric scooter market for investors. You have limited time. Do you start top-down from transportation spend data, or bottom-up from individual rider behavior and unit economics?

options.text: Top-down: faster, gives a credible ballpark from industry data
Bottom-up: more defensible, shows you understand the business
Skip sizing and focus on competitor revenue benchmarks
Use both approaches and triangulate for a stronger estimate

interactions.prompt: Two analysts size the US meditation app market. Analyst A: 330M people × 10% meditate × $100/yr = $3.3B. Analyst B: 50M smartphone wellness users × 8% pay × $80/yr = $320M. Which is SAM vs TAM?

options.text: A is closer to TAM; B is closer to SAM
A is SAM; B is SOM
Both are calculating TAM differently
B is TAM; A is SAM

chartData.title: Market Size Estimates: TAM vs SAM

interactions.prompt: Rank these market sizing steps in the correct order when building a bottom-up estimate for a new coffee subscription service.

options.text: Multiply by average revenue per subscriber per year
Identify the target customer segment (e.g., urban millennials)
Estimate realistic conversion rate from segment to paying customers
Calculate total addressable population in your launch geography

interactions.prompt: Your team is pitching a B2B SaaS tool for dentists. Marketing says TAM is $15B (all healthcare SaaS). Sales says SAM is $400M (dental practices only). Which number leads the pitch deck?

options.text: Lead with $15B TAM  -  investors want big markets
Lead with $400M SAM  -  it's credible and specific to your product
Show both but anchor on SAM with a clear path to expand
Show only SOM to appear conservative and trustworthy

interactions.prompt: Rank these data sources from MOST to LEAST reliable when sizing the US online tutoring market top-down.

options.text: A competitor's self-reported press release claiming market leadership
US Census data on school-age population and household income
IBISWorld or Statista industry report on online education spending
A Quora thread estimating the tutoring market

interactions.prompt: Post-COVID, remote work becomes permanent for 30% of US workers. Your commuter coffee cart business had a SOM of $2M based on downtown foot traffic. How do you adjust?

options.text: Reduce SOM by ~30% to reflect lower downtown foot traffic
Keep SOM the same  -  coffee demand doesn't change
Resize SAM to include suburban/home delivery, then re-estimate SOM
Abandon the market entirely since it's shrinking

interactions.priorContext: You originally sized the commuter coffee cart market assuming pre-COVID foot traffic in downtown business districts. Now 30% of workers are permanently remote, fundamentally changing where your customers are.
